idea: A pre-order page for a café's morning pastries.

decision: What counts as success for the pre-order page
options: Completed pre-orders picked up per day
Page visits to order conversion rate
Revenue from pre-orders
recommendation: Completed pre-orders picked up per day
reason: Picked-up orders show the page really works for the café and customers, and one number is enough to decide on extras.

decision: Which customer details to store with each order, and for how long
options: Name and pickup time only, deleted after 30 days
Name, phone and email, kept indefinitely
Name and phone, deleted after pickup plus 7 days
recommendation: Name and phone, deleted after pickup plus 7 days
reason: A phone number is the only detail needed to reach someone about a missed or changed order, and keeping it longer has no decision behind it.

decision: Which order events to track
options: Only placed and picked-up orders
Placed, picked-up and no-show orders plus abandoned checkouts
Every click on the page
recommendation: Placed, picked-up and no-show orders plus abandoned checkouts
reason: These four events answer whether people finish ordering and whether they show up, and nothing else on the page changes a decision.

note: Defined what the pre-order page records: success measure, customer contact data and its retention, and the order events worth tracking.

decision: How to stop two people ordering the last pastry
options: Atomic stock decrement in the database at order time
Check stock on page load only
Let orders through and fix by hand
recommendation: Atomic stock decrement in the database at order time
reason: A single conditional update on the count is plain, proven, and guarantees nobody is promised a pastry that's gone.

decision: Whether customers pay online or at pickup
options: Pay at pickup, no online payment
Pay online with a hosted checkout
Card hold online, charge at pickup
recommendation: Pay at pickup, no online payment
reason: It is the smallest version that works end to end and avoids handling money, refunds, and card data.

decision: How customers get their order confirmation
options: Confirmation on screen plus an email
On-screen confirmation only
Text message
recommendation: Confirmation on screen plus an email
reason: Email is cheap and reliable, and gives the customer a record to show at pickup.

note: Engineering decisions for a café morning-pastry pre-order page: stock limits, payment, and order confirmation.

decision: What happens when a pastry sells out
options: Show sold out, no waitlist
Waitlist with auto-offer on cancellation
Hide sold-out items
reason: A leisure centre waitlist exists for full classes (unverified, page not opened), but it does not show pastry buyers want one, so the smallest version just says sold out.

decision: Cutoff time for ordering and for cancelling
options: Order until the night before, no cancellations
Order until an hour before pickup, cancel until then
Order until a fixed time each morning
recommendation: Order until the night before, no cancellations
reason: We'd learn first how the café bakes (batch size, prep time) and how often customers change plans, since the finding says nothing about food.

decision: Whether customers pay online or at pickup
options: Pay at pickup
Pay online when ordering
Card hold now, charge at pickup
reason: We'd learn first how many no-shows the café sees; paying at pickup is the smallest working version and avoids handling money and refunds.

note: Listed the key pre-order decisions for the café pastry page: sell-out handling, order cutoff, and payment timing, noting what is known and what to learn first.

decision: How the customer picks a pickup time
options: Fixed pickup slots (e.g. every 15 min)
Free-text time field
Just 'tomorrow morning', no time
reason: Slots keep the café's morning rush manageable and are the smallest thing that works end to end.

decision: What the page shows when a pastry sells out
options: Show it greyed out with 'Sold out'
Hide it from the list
Let people order and confirm later
recommendation: Show it greyed out with 'Sold out'
reason: Customers see what exists and aren't promised something the café can't bake.

decision: How the pastry list is laid out
options: One simple list with photo, name, price and a plus button
Grouped by category (sweet, savoury, etc.) with tabs
Photo grid
recommendation: One simple list with photo, name, price and a plus button
reason: A short morning menu doesn't need categories, and a single list is fastest to build and to scan on a phone.

note: Sketched the pre-order page structure: how pastries are listed, how pickup is chosen, and what the customer sees after ordering.

decision: How the page handles pastries that sell out or hit the daily limit
options: Fixed daily cap per item with 'sold out' label only
Show live remaining count and disable sold-out items
Let orders through and café confirms later
Show a fixed daily cap per item with 'sold out' label only
recommendation: Fixed daily cap per item with 'sold out' label only
reason: A simple cap per item avoids promising what the kitchen can't bake and is the smallest version that works end to end.

decision: What pickup time and order cutoff the customer is asked for
options: Pick a pickup time slot
Just choose a pickup day, collect any time during morning hours
Pick a time window (e.g. 7–8, 8–9)
recommendation: Just choose a pickup day, collect any time during morning hours
reason: Slots add capacity logic the café must manage, while a day plus a clear cutoff time the night before is enough to start.

decision: What happens when a customer wants to change or cancel an order
options: No changes online; customer calls or messages the café
Free cancel until the cutoff via a link
No cancellations at all
recommendation: No changes online; customer calls or messages the café
reason: Self-serve cancel is extra to build and the policy shown to customers is a promise, so start with a plain contact line in the customer's words.
